knowledge:
- key_parameters: statisticType=The statistical metric to compute (e.g., "tstatistic") ;; referenceGroupLabel=The baseline group label in the sample metadata (e.g., "normal") ;; retain.chrs=The chromosomes to include in the analysis (e.g., 1:22 to focus on autosomes) ;; reference_position_type=The method to define a single coordinate per feature (e.g., "median", "start", "end", "strand.start", "end.start") ;; sortAndCleanNA=Logical indicating whether to sort data by chromosomal coordinates and remove NA values ;; qval.threshold=The adjusted p-value threshold for identifying significant genomic regions ;; smoothStatistic.tail=The tail of the smoothed statistic to extract (e.g., "upper" for positive peaks/upregulation, "lower" for negative peaks/downregulation) ;; smoothStatistic.threshold=The minimum absolute value of the smoothed statistic required to filter out false positives ;; outputGenomicAnnotationsForPREDA=An optional parameter in PREDA_main to project copy number results onto the same reference positions as gene expression data
- alternatives: justRMA or rma from the affy package can be used to preprocess raw Affymetrix CEL files before PREDA analysis ;; Custom gene-centered CDF definitions (e.g., GeneAnnot or Brainarray) are preferred over standard Affymetrix CDFs to improve probe-to-position mapping accuracy and reduce noise
- when_to_use: Use this package when you want to identify genomic regions with localized, coordinated changes in quantitative functional genomics data (such as regional gene expression changes or copy number alterations) rather than analyzing features in isolation
- pitfalls: Running position-related analysis on sex chromosomes (X and Y) is discouraged because unbalanced male/female sample ratios in the dataset can bias the results ;; Using standard Affymetrix CDFs instead of custom gene-centered CDFs can yield noisier position-related results due to multiple probesets mapping to the same gene locus ;; High permutation counts (nperms, default 10000) are computationally intensive; parallel computing (parallelComputations=TRUE) requires proper installation of Rmpi and rsprng

workflows.name: diff_expressed_regions
workflows.intent: Identify chromosomal regions with significant localized up- or down-regulation of gene expression.
input: sampleinfoGE_PREDA.txt (sample metadata file containing array names, sample names, and classes)
Raw Affymetrix .CEL files or an ExpressionSet object
workflows.stages:
1. Compute differential expression statistics from an ExpressionSet using statisticsForPREDAfromEset.
2. Retrieve genomic annotations using eset2GenomicAnnotations.
3. Convert annotations to a PREDA-compatible format with reference positions using GenomicAnnotations2GenomicAnnotationsForPREDA.
4. Merge statistics and annotations into a single DataForPREDA object using MergeStatisticAnnotations2DataForPREDA.
5. Run the core smoothing and permutation analysis using PREDA_main.
6. Extract significant genomic regions using PREDAResults2GenomicRegions.
7. Convert the identified regions to a dataframe using GenomicRegions2dataframe.
8. Plot the significant regions along the chromosomes using genomePlot.
workflows.code:
GEstatisticsForPREDA<-statisticsForPREDAfromEset(ExpressionSetRCC, statisticType="tstatistic", referenceGroupLabel="normal", classVector=sampleinfo[,"Class"])
GEGenomicAnnotations<-eset2GenomicAnnotations(ExpressionSetRCC, retain.chrs=1:22)
GEGenomicAnnotationsForPREDA<-GenomicAnnotations2GenomicAnnotationsForPREDA(GEGenomicAnnotations, reference_position_type="median")
GEDataForPREDA<-MergeStatisticAnnotations2DataForPREDA(GEstatisticsForPREDA, GEGenomicAnnotationsForPREDA, sortAndCleanNA=TRUE)
GEanalysisResults<-PREDA_main(GEDataForPREDA)
genomic_regions_UP<-PREDAResults2GenomicRegions(GEanalysisResults, qval.threshold=0.05, smoothStatistic.tail="upper", smoothStatistic.threshold=0.5)
genomic_regions_DOWN<-PREDAResults2GenomicRegions(GEanalysisResults, qval.threshold=0.05, smoothStatistic.tail="lower", smoothStatistic.threshold=(-0.5))
dataframe_UPregions<-GenomicRegions2dataframe(genomic_regions_UP[[1]])
checkplot<-genomePlot(GEanalysisResults, genomicRegions=c(genomic_regions_UP, genomic_regions_DOWN), grouping=c(1, 1), scale.positions="Mb", region.colors=c("red","blue"))

workflows.name: sodegir_combined_analysis
workflows.intent: Integrate gene expression and copy number data to identify genomic regions with significant overlapping alterations (amplified/deleted regions) across multiple samples.
input: sampleinfoGE_PREDA.txt (sample metadata file for gene expression)
workflows.stages:
1. Preprocess gene expression data for SODEGIR using SODEGIRpreprocessingGE.
2. Run PREDA analysis on gene expression data using PREDA_main.
3. Extract significant up- and down-regulated expression regions using PREDAResults2GenomicRegions.
4. Import copy number statistics from file using StatisticsForPREDAFromfile.
5. Import copy number genomic annotations from file using GenomicAnnotationsForPREDAFromfile.
6. Merge copy number statistics and annotations using MergeStatisticAnnotations2DataForPREDA.
7. Run PREDA analysis on copy number data, projecting onto gene expression reference positions, using PREDA_main.
8. Extract copy number gain and loss regions using PREDAResults2GenomicRegions.
9. Find overlapping regions (amplified and deleted) using GenomicRegionsFindOverlap.
10. Plot integrated results using genomePlot.
11. Compute dataset-level signatures of recurrent alterations using computeDatasetSignature.
workflows.code:
SODEGIRGEDataForPREDA<-SODEGIRpreprocessingGE(AffyBatchInput=AffybatchRCC, custom_cdfname="hgu133plus2", classColumn="Class", referenceGroupLabel="normal", statisticType="tstatistic", optionalAnnotations=c("SYMBOL", "ENTREZID"), retain.chrs=1:22)
SODEGIRGEanalysisResults<-PREDA_main(SODEGIRGEDataForPREDA)
SODEGIR_GE_UP<-PREDAResults2GenomicRegions(SODEGIRGEanalysisResults, qval.threshold=0.05, smoothStatistic.tail="upper", smoothStatistic.threshold=0.5)
SODEGIR_GE_DOWN<-PREDAResults2GenomicRegions(SODEGIRGEanalysisResults, qval.threshold=0.05, smoothStatistic.tail="lower", smoothStatistic.threshold= -0.5)
CNStatisticsForPREDA<-StatisticsForPREDAFromfile(file=CNdataFile, ids_column="AffymetrixSNPsID", testedTail="both", sep="\t", header=TRUE)
CNGenomicsAnnotationsForPREDA<-GenomicAnnotationsForPREDAFromfile(file=CNannotationFile, ids_column=1, chr_column="Chromosome", start_column=4, end_column=4, strand_column="Strand", chromosomesLabelsInput=1:22, MinusStrandString="-", PlusStrandString="+", optionalAnnotationsColumns=c("Cytoband", "Entrez_gene"), header=TRUE, sep=",", quote="\"", na.strings = c("NA", "", "---"))
SODEGIRCNDataForPREDA<-MergeStatisticAnnotations2DataForPREDA(CNStatisticsForPREDA, CNGenomicsAnnotationsForPREDA, sortAndCleanNA=TRUE, quiet=FALSE, MedianCenter=TRUE)
SODEGIRCNanalysisResults<-PREDA_main(SODEGIRCNDataForPREDA, outputGenomicAnnotationsForPREDA=SODEGIRGEDataForPREDA)
SODEGIR_CN_GAIN<-PREDAResults2GenomicRegions(SODEGIRCNanalysisResults, qval.threshold=0.01, smoothStatistic.tail="upper", smoothStatistic.threshold=0.1)
SODEGIR_CN_LOSS<-PREDAResults2GenomicRegions(SODEGIRCNanalysisResults, qval.threshold=0.01, smoothStatistic.tail="lower", smoothStatistic.threshold= -0.1)
SODEGIR_AMPLIFIED<-GenomicRegionsFindOverlap(SODEGIR_GE_UP, SODEGIR_CN_GAIN)
SODEGIR_DELETED<-GenomicRegionsFindOverlap(SODEGIR_GE_DOWN, SODEGIR_CN_LOSS)
names(SODEGIR_AMPLIFIED)<-names(SODEGIR_GE_UP)
names(SODEGIR_DELETED)<-names(SODEGIR_GE_DOWN)
regions_forPlot<-c(SODEGIR_GE_UP[[1]],SODEGIR_CN_GAIN[[1]],SODEGIR_AMPLIFIED[[1]],SODEGIR_GE_DOWN[[1]],SODEGIR_CN_LOSS[[1]],SODEGIR_DELETED[[1]])
checkplot<-genomePlot(SODEGIRGEanalysisResults, genomicRegions=regions_forPlot, grouping=c(1:3, 1:3), scale.positions="Mb", region.colors=c("red","red2","red4","blue","blue2","blue4"))
SDGsignature_amplified<-computeDatasetSignature(SODEGIRGEDataForPREDA, genomicRegionsList=SODEGIR_AMPLIFIED)
SDGsignature_deleted<-computeDatasetSignature(SODEGIRGEDataForPREDA, genomicRegionsList=SODEGIR_DELETED)
